text:
Maya (PM): heads-up — Competitor Atlas rolled out a feature yesterday that they’re marketing as 'instant routing' for sub-100ms p95 at ~50% cost. getting pressure from sales to react. do we treat this as parity or double-down on our differentiators?
Conner (Eng): saw the post. sounds like a combination of aggressive pre-warming + a tiny model variant. their claims look suspicious at scale.
Sophie (Research): dug into their repo/notes. they appear to precompute KV caches and do short-context truncation for certain routes. quality likely drops on long chats.
Arjun (Sales): Acme just pinged me asking if we can match that. they framed it as a blocker for their renewal. they want a timeline.
Maya (PM): options I see: 1) quick parity shim (spike to emulate their routing + caching) 2) lean into our positioning: controlled latency SLOs + cost telemetry + Dedicated guarantees 3) offer targeted pilot with docs/guidance. need engineering cost/risks to decide.
Conner (Eng): quick estimates: parity spike = 2 engs x 2 sprints to prototype a routing shim + prefix pre-warm; production hardening another 1-2 sprints + infra review. risks: memory pressure, cross-tenant caching concerns for hosted.
Li (ML): model-side impacts: you can compress context and prune attention to save tokens but expect hallucination/regression on convo continuity. we'd need evaluation against customer prompts.
Sophie (Research): propose a 48h mini-eval: 500 customer-like prompts across 3 workloads, measure ROUGE/fidelity + latency. can run on staging variants.
Maya (PM): suggested launch criteria for a parity-lite feature: a) p95 within 10% of their claim on our customers' traffic profile, b) no >2% regression on quality evals, c) cost delta <= 1.2x current baseline. if we can't meet, fallback = pilot + docs.
Arjun (Sales): Acme is flexible — would do a 6-week pilot if we can show staging numbers. that buys us time to decide whether to ship.
Conner (Eng): I'll start a spike branch. initial plan: implement a routing policy + caching layer that honors tenant isolation. sample command to run locally:\n```\n# run local spike\npython -m infra.runner --config spikes/parity_routing.yaml --warm-prefix 128\n```\nConner (Eng): notes: we'll need eng-runtime and eng-platform signoff if we surface this to hosted. security concern: ensure no KV leakage between tenants.
Sophie (Research): starting the eval now. will post results as a short table in this thread.
deploy-bot: Deployed branch/maya-parity-spike to staging at 2064001600
Maya (PM): decision: greenlight spike only. product wont commit to GA until we see eval + perf + cost. reconvene Fri @ 10am. any objections?
Arjun (Sales): no objections. will coordinate Acme pilot if numbers look reasonable.
Li (ML): no objections. will monitor for quality regressions.
Conner (Eng): tagging @eng-runtime @eng-platform for scope. will add a short RFC by end of day.
Sophie (Research): will drop eval link here in ~36h.
Maya (PM): thanks all. target outcomes for Friday: 1) perf numbers on staging vs controlled baseline 2) quality delta report 3) rough cost estimate + rollout risk list. :thumbsup:
